critiques.target: Epoch accounting (H1.1.2, H1.4.1, H4.2.1, H4.2.2, H2.3.1, E004–E016 descriptions)
critiques.issue: The epoch labels look wrong by about 1. E004 runs at 9.04 s, which is the compiled version of E002's 10-epoch run (−14% from 10.39 s). E005 adds only +0.6% to that, so it is also a 10-epoch run, not 9. E012's per-epoch CUDA timings have 10 entries: nine full epochs and a final 466 ms ≈ 0.52 × 888 ms. So the tip runs about 9.5 epochs, not the 8.5 the logs claim. H1.3.2 already flagged 'time suggests 10, not 9' and nobody checked. Every hypothesis worded 'at 9 epochs fixed', and every comparison against reference epoch counts (airbench96 at 9, the iterate-futurebiohackers slope), is anchored to the wrong number.
critiques.suggestion: Read the epoch and step count from the E016 commit, or log total steps ÷ steps per epoch. Rewrite the affected hypotheses in true epochs, or better in optimizer steps, since batch size changed from 1024 to 2000 at E006. Then recompute the per-epoch slopes.

critiques.issue: E009 says it runs 'On the E007 recipe at 9 epochs'. But its time (6.99 s) matches E008 (6.98 s), not E007 (7.33 s), and the outcome is computed against E008. Either the description is wrong or the comparison is. Separately, H1.3.4 is still 'open, 0.35' although its own pre-registered test (≥0.3 pp) failed with −0.08 pp.
critiques.suggestion: Fix the E009 description to match the base it actually used. Mark H1.3.4 refuted. Retire H1.3.3 (LR floor without EMA): EMA is now always on, so the answer can't affect the recipe.

critiques.issue: Many statuses contradict their evidence. H1.3.1 is open after E013 refuted it. H2.2.2 is open (0.30) after E015 measured −0.9% against a ≥3% claim. H2.3.1 is open after E007 refuted it. H3.3 and H3.3.1 are open after E012 measured ~60 ms of first-epoch overhead against a 0.3 s claim. H4.1.1 is open after E012 gave bit-identical accuracies with time within 0.1%. H1.5.2 and H4.2.2 are open after supporting results. H2 is open although compile (−14%), resizing (−22%) and width (−5%) all landed inside its 10–25% claim. In the other direction, H2.3 carries only E011−, while E007 (the biggest single time win) is not attached to it.
critiques.suggestion: Sync statuses with the evidence: refute H1.3.1, H1.3.4, H2.2.2, H2.3.1, H3.3 and H3.3.1. Support H4.1.1 (on the no-cudagraph artifact), H1.5.2, H4.2.2 and H2. Add E007+ to H2.3 and restate it as 'resolution is a near-linear time dial with an accuracy cliff below ~24 px or a <30% full-res tail'.

critiques.issue: The data already contradicts this. Prepare costs 0.06–0.21 s, the first epoch carries ~60 ms of overhead only in trial 0, and E011 puts fixed per-step overhead at ~5% of train time in total. Fixed epoch-independent cost is ~1–2% of 6.6 s. Keeping H3 open at 0.20 invites more work on a lever that is worth at most ~0.1 s.
critiques.suggestion: Refute H3 (cite E012 and E004's per-trial prepare times) and close its subtree. The one exception is the 0.15 s prepare cost in trial 0, which build could pre-warm cheaply. If anything is kept, make it a single small Lvl3 for that.

critiques.target: E016 / H1.5.1 (wd halving, kept as tip)
critiques.issue: The new margin (+0.77 pp) rests on one 3-seed run. Against E015 it is about 1.6σ, and E015's own +0.26 pp was declared kernel noise. The post-mortem's mechanism (BN biases decayed at 64× lr) is an untested story. wd was halved on every group, so the gain could equally come from the Muon filters: under Muon the update norm is fixed, so wd sets the equilibrium weight norm and therefore the effective LR. This is also the margin the next epoch trim will spend.
critiques.suggestion: Before trimming, rerun E016 offline on held-out seeds 3–12, as E012 did (~70 s). Then split the effect into two runs: halve wd only on the SGD/BN-bias groups, and only on the Muon filters. Add each as a Lvl3 under H1.5 so the post-mortem's mechanism becomes falsifiable.

critiques.issue: '~0.36 pp/epoch' and '1.4 vs 1.9 s/pp, so width is a worse dial than epochs' both come from single 3-seed differences of 0.18 and 0.25 pp. The SE of a 3-seed difference is ~0.2 pp, so neither slope is resolved and the ranking of dials is not supported. The planned trim will lean on these slopes.
critiques.suggestion: Treat the slopes as unknown to within ±100%. Make the next trim a two-point sweep on E016, for example −0.5 and −1.0 true epochs. That gives a slope from more than one difference and shows which point still clears 0.753 with ≥0.15 pp to spare.

critiques.issue: E006 changed two things at once: SGD to Muon, and batch size 1024 to 2000, which halves the steps per epoch. The +0.66 pp can't be credited to Muon. H1.2.1's claims (≥10% fewer epochs than tuned SGD, ≥5% less time) were never tested. SGD was never tuned, Muon was never trimmed alone, and E006 was 3.8% slower. Yet E006 is logged as '+' and H1.2 sits at 0.25 confidence while Muon is in every recipe since. Momentum 0.6 and the number of Newton-Schulz iterations were never varied, and the NS overhead (+3.8%) is the largest per-step cost left.
critiques.suggestion: Run one deconfounding test on the current tip: Muon at batch size 1024, or SGD at batch size 2000. Add cheap Lvl3s for 3 NS iterations instead of 5 (≈1–2% time) and for Muon momentum 0.8/0.9. Re-score H1.2.1 as inconclusive until one of these runs.

critiques.issue: The '4× loss per pixel saved' was blamed on the resolution schedule. There is an alternative nobody checked: the Lookahead/EMA copy and the BN running stats average over low-resolution phases. With a shorter 32 px tail (20% instead of 30%), more of the averaged weights and BN statistics come from 20–28 px inputs, which the model never sees at eval. That would make the cliff partly an end-of-run calibration problem rather than a feature-learning one. H1.3.6 (BN recalibration) is untested and is exactly the test.
critiques.suggestion: Run H1.3.6 on the current tip: recalibrate BN at 32 px on ≤5k training images after the EMA swap, timed. If it helps, re-test the single-factor resize variant the post-mortem itself recommended (add a 20 px phase, keep the 30% tail), with recalibration on.

critiques.issue: The tree has no live hypothesis on the levers that remain. H2.4 (proxy-based hard-example selection, the main source of airbench96_faster's speed) is untouched at 0.12. Yet E011 shows ~95% of time is pixel-proportional forward/backward work, which is exactly what skipping half the backward pass removes. Other untested levers: the widths of groups 1 and 2, convs per group (3→2), batch size alone, EMA schedule and frequency, warm-up length, and alternating vs random flip (H1.4.1). H1.1.2 (whitening ablation) is a scientific question with no plausible time payoff.
critiques.suggestion: Promote H2.4.1 to the queue after the epoch trim, since it is the only untested idea with a ≥10% upside. Add one Lvl3 for depth (2 convs per group) and one for the group-2 width. Deprioritize or retire H1.1.2 and H1.4.1.

critiques.target: H4.1 / E015 (determinism and the judging GPU)
critiques.issue: E015 showed that changing compile mode re-runs autotuning and shifts every seed's trajectory. The official judge is an A100 PCIe: different clocks and power limit, and its own max-autotune pass in build. Kernel choices there will likely differ, so the local 3-seed accuracy is one trajectory sample, not the judged value. E012 established bit-identity only for the no-cudagraph artifact. Also, keep decisions made on seeds 0–2 (E013, E014, E016, all within 2σ) select seed noise; E012 already found the 3-seed mean 0.08 pp optimistic. No Lvl1 covers transfer from the SXM4 machine to the PCIe judge.
critiques.suggestion: Test H4.1.1 on the cudagraph (max-autotune) recipe with a fresh build process twice. If kernel picks vary between builds, budget an extra ~0.15 pp of margin. Add a Lvl1 or Lvl2 on transfer to the judge: the time ranking holds on a power-limited PCIe card because the step is GPU-bound, and accuracy must be judged as the 40-seed mean, with ≥0.3 pp headroom over 0.75.

critiques.issue: E015's post-mortem argues the step is GPU-bound and that ~5% overhead is the ceiling. But no one measured how efficient the conv kernels are (achieved TFLOPs, i.e. MFU, at 24/28/32 px with batch 2000). The 32 px epoch takes 0.89 s, ~56k img/s, which may be well below the A100's fp16 peak for this net. 'GPU-bound' could still mean poor kernels, not a lack of headroom.
critiques.suggestion: Add a diagnostic Lvl3: profile one 32 px step and compute the achieved FLOP rate. If MFU is under ~40%, open a branch on kernel efficiency: channel widths aligned to tensor-core tiles, bf16 vs fp16, and cuDNN vs Triton conv picks under max-autotune.

structured_output.summary: The record has improved, but several key conclusions are weaker than the tree claims. (1) The epoch counts in the logs look off by about 1: compute time and the 10-entry per-epoch timing in E012 imply E004/E005 run 10 epochs and the tip runs ~9.5, not 9/8.5. Every hypothesis anchored to '9 epochs' is mis-specified, and E009's description contradicts its own time and baseline. (2) The current margin (E016, +0.77 pp) rests on one 3-seed run at ~1.6σ, with an untested and confounded mechanism (wd was halved on both the Muon filters and the BN biases). The slopes used to decide how far to trim (E008's 0.36 pp/epoch, E010's s/pp exchange rates) are single differences inside the ~0.2 pp noise of a 3-seed difference. Validate E016 on held-out seeds and run a two-point epoch trim before spending that margin. (3) Muon's credit is confounded with the batch-size change from 1024 to 2000. H1.2.1's actual claims were never tested, yet it is logged as support. (4) Many statuses lag the evidence. H1.3.1, H1.3.4, H2.2.2, H2.3.1, H3.3 and H3.3.1 should be refuted. H3 as a whole is contradicted (fixed overhead is ~1–2%). H2, H1.5.2, H4.2.2 and H4.1.1 should be supported. E007, the largest single time win, is not attached to H2.3 as support. (5) E011's resolution 'cliff' has an unexamined alternative: EMA weights and BN stats contaminated by low-res phases. BN recalibration (H1.3.6) is the test. (6) Untried levers with real upside: hard-example selection (H2.4, which targets the ~95% of time that scales with pixels), depth and group-1/2 widths, NS iteration count, Muon momentum, and a kernel-efficiency (MFU) diagnostic. (7) No hypothesis covers transfer to the PCIe judge, where re-autotuned kernels change the per-seed trajectories, or selection bias from keep decisions made on seeds 0–2.
